subject: Annual planning: Resilience targets & scenario playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Annual planning: Resilience targets & scenario playbook

Team —

We need to kick off annual planning with a focused run on resilience scenarios and target banding. Goal: produce a 3-tier set of ARR/CAC/latency targets (base / stress / conservative) and a short playbook that maps remediation levers to each scenario. This will feed QBR narratives and leadership asks.

Key asks for this week:
- Review the attached planning-template.xlsx and suggest any missing KPIs by EOD Thursday.
- I want a 90-minute working session on Thu 11 Feb 11:00–12:30 PT to align on scenario definitions and owner mapping. Please accept the invite if you can make it.
- Laura: can you pull last-year variance by product line (net new ARR, churn, infra spend) and bucket into the template?
- Vivek: draft a short ops SLA risk matrix (3 failure modes) we can show the execs.
- Tessa: own the QBR outline and final slide deck.

We’ll loop in Finance and a small external customer panel after leadership aligns on ranges. I’ve attached a scenario-matrix draft and an initial QBR outline.

Thanks — let’s keep this lean.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
VP, Product & Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: planning-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), scenario-matrix.pdf (pdf), QBR-outline.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning: Resilience targets & scenario playbook

On Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 9:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> We need to kick off annual planning with a focused run on resilience scenarios and target banding...

Thanks, Soojin — I’ve started pulling the FY26 vs FY27 delta by product line and will populate the "revenue movements" tab in the template. Two quick notes:
1) Should we include a row for Dedicated contracts with committed throughput vs actual usage? That’s where most of the variance is, and it affects infrastructure allocation.
2) I propose we add a short "customer confidence" KPI (Net Promoter downtick) tied to latency SLO breaches; it's small but leadership cares.

I’ll have a first-pass fill by Thursday 4pm PT. Accepting the invite now.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning: Resilience targets & scenario playbook

Thanks, Soojin.

I sketched an ops SLA risk matrix and attached a short note. High level: three failure modes to consider — (A) GPU supply shock, (B) Multi-region networking outage, (C) Regressions from model rollout. For each, I mapped mitigations (burst capacity, cross-region failover, canary/rollback policies).

Question: do you want the conservative scenario to assume a 25% traffic surge for 6 weeks, or should we model a 50% surge but with partial fallbacks (i.e., degrade to smaller quantized variants)? My gut says model both and treat the 25% as our baseline stress test.

— Vivek
Sr. Director, Infrastructure

Attachments: ops-risk-matrix.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning: Resilience targets & scenario playbook

Accepted the invite.

Quick note: I expanded the QBR-outline.docx into a 6-slide narrative: current state, key risks (top 3), target bands, investments required, playbook (who does what), and exec ask. I'll upload the slide draft to Drive after the session.

Also tagging a potential external panel: Maya Gupta (Atlas Retail) asked to review our resilience commitments last quarter — should we invite one customer to validate the playbook assumptions before finalizing?

— Tessa
Head of Customer Success

Attachments: none

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 13:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning: Resilience targets & scenario playbook

Great — thanks everyone.

Decision notes from the working session:
- Base / Stress / Conservative bands agreed: Base = flat growth assumptions, Stress = +25% traffic surge, Conservative = +50% with partial fallback.
- Laura will model P&L impact under each band (including incremental infra and increased credits).
- Vivek will quantify latency delta and cost delta for fallback paths (quantized models).
- Tessa will draft the customer validation plan; we’ll ask Maya for 30 minutes the week of Feb 22.
- Deadline: leadership slide deck ready by Fri Feb 19 for pre-read.

Action items are in the Drive folder (link below). I pushed a cleaned scenario-matrix to the folder.

On the customer invite: yes, loop in Maya for a sanity check — keep the ask focused (validate whether the tradeoffs match their tolerance).

— Soojin

Attachments: scenario-matrix-v2.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPlanResilience

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cfo-atlas.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@atlasretail.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning: Resilience targets & scenario playbook

Hi Soojin / Tessa —

Thanks for the invite. Maya forwarded the session notes and we appreciate the transparency on fallback costs. A couple of asks from our side for the customer sanity check:
- Please highlight the customer impact under the Conservative band in plain terms (expected degradation in latency and features).
- If you propose credits or contractual concessions tied to fallback usage, include a short example calculation.

We can spare 30 minutes the week of Feb 22; Maya will send calendar times.

Best,
Jordan Price
Interim CFO, Atlas Retail

Attachments: none
